page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is a memory-oriented general purpose virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 31 GB of RAM. The compute resources are powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C x86_64 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside cryptographic extensions. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark results reveal strong single-thread performance contrasting with aggregate multi-core limits inherent to a 4-vCPU footprint. The system achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2258.0 points and single-threaded gzip compression of 35.11 GB/sec. Text processing workloads similarly achieve top-decile throughput at 2843.0 points. Conversely, total compute benchmarks reflect the low core count, resulting in a multi-core Geekbench score of 5040.0 points and a PassMark CPU score of 6350.73. Potentially uncached 256 MB memory bandwidth tests measure 32.39 GB/sec for read and 20.69 GB/sec for write operations, while Redis SET throughput benchmarks at 4.9 million operations per second.

With 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance profile offers high resource density for memory-dependent tasks without necessitating unnecessary core scaling. Cost efficiency remains favorable for workloads bottlenecked on memory capacity or single-threaded execution rather than raw multi-core throughput. Fitting workloads include in-memory caching tiers, single-threaded processing pipelines, small-to-medium relational databases requiring generous buffer pools, and web serving architectures.

Driven by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz with AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, it features 260 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Performance benchmarks highlight exceptional single-threaded capabilities, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2258.0 and strong compression throughput, while overall multi-threaded scores remain constrained by the low core allocation. Its memory density makes it cost-efficient for workloads requiring significant RAM without paying for excess compute cores. It is suited for in-memory databases, caching services, web serving, and memory-intensive single-threaded processing tasks.
